alternative_rejected.option: Merge fleet_claim_corridor.py and fleet_claims.py into one module
alternative_rejected.rejection_evidence: fleet_claim_corridor.py is v0 path-level claim substrate with macOS xattr mirrors and separate consumer surface (FleetClaimLedger + FleetClaimProtocol). fleet_claims.py is workspace-scoped claim authority with different event schema and jsonschema validation. Merging would break both consumer surfaces. The correct approach: declare fleet_claims.py canonical for workspace claims, keep corridor as legacy path-level substrate adapted through typed re-exports.

alternative_rejected.option: Implement full two-phase commit for FleetClaimStore + WorkspaceLedger writes
alternative_rejected.rejection_evidence: Two-phase commit requires a coordinator, prepare/commit phases, and distributed consensus. Overkill for local single-process claim operations. Compensation-based approach (try/except + release on failure) is appropriate for the single-machine, single-process use case and matches the existing _transition rollback pattern.

strongest_suspected_weakness: First-transition cache corruption in recover(): when the first _transition (RECOVERED) fails, session_id and head_sha are set on cached but the failure path returns without restoring original values. The in-memory cache retains the new session_id despite the recovery failing. On the next call, the warm cache returns a workspace seemingly recovered. Mitigated by the fact that _save_workspace was never called (state on disk is correct), and the next _transition call would reload from disk on cache miss. A future slice should add explicit cache restoration in the first-transition failure path.
proposed_reviewer_attack_surface: First-transition cache corruption: session_id not restored on failure
Triple-failure save at recover() line 740: unguarded rollback _save_workspace
verify_chain() never invoked in production service path — evidence integrity checks offline only
_load_all() skips ledger validation on service restart
Concurrent recovery lock only protects recovery-vs-recovery, not recovery-vs-mutation
Dual-write compensation: if re-acquisition in release_boundary_claim fails, claim is permanently lost
No authorization layer for workspace operations (any caller can acquire claims, retire workspaces)
